seoTitle: Boise School District Calendar: Key Dates & Official PDFs
seoDescription: Reviewed Boise School District dates, Pre-K and ECSE exceptions, grade-band conferences, early-release times, breaks, and official student PDFs.
districtFact: Boise School District's one-page student calendar combines 176 instructional days with unusually specific operational details: K–12 begins and ends on early-release schedules, Pre-K and ECSE use separate opening and ending dates, fall conferences affect grade bands differently, and elementary dismissal time depends on whether the campus follows the standard or transportation-driven late-start schedule.

about.title: The First and Last Days Are Early Release
about.content: Boise's K–12 calendar does not begin with a full day. Both reviewed years open on August 12 with early release and close in May with another early-release day. Standard elementary schools dismiss at 1:15 p.m.; the campuses listed on the district's late-start schedule dismiss at 1:45 p.m.; junior highs dismiss at noon when elementary students also release early; and senior highs dismiss at 12:30 p.m.

about.title: Pre-K and ECSE Follow Different Edges of the Year
about.content: Pre-K and Early Childhood Special Education programs start several days after K–12 and finish before the districtwide K–12 last day. Pre-K is also excluded on some reporting and conference dates when older students attend, so early-childhood families need the program labels rather than a generic first-day or last-day answer.

about.title: Fall Conferences Change by Grade Band
about.content: Boise schedules elementary, junior-high, and high-school evening conferences on different dates. The daytime closure applies to Pre-K through grade 6, while secondary conferences occur in the evening; the following Friday is a districtwide no-school day. Families with children at multiple levels should plan from the conference table, not one districtwide label.

about.title: A Historic Urban District with Multiple Pathways
about.content: Boise's first public school dates to 1863, the district says it has served families since 1865, and Independent School District of Boise City #1 was created in 1881. Today the official site highlights dual language immersion, Montessori, magnet programs, Boise Online School, and career-technical study alongside neighborhood schools.

calendarNotes: The Boise student calendar lists 176 instructional days divided into four reporting periods of 42, 43, 47, and 44 days. K–12 begins August 12 with early release, while Pre-K and ECSE begin later. Seniors, Pre-K, and ECSE finish before the K–11 last day. October conference schedules vary across elementary, junior-high, and high-school levels, and only Pre-K through grade 6 have the daytime conference closure. Standard and late-start elementary campuses use different early-release times because the district coordinates transportation schedules. Junior-high early-release time also changes depending on whether elementary schools release early that day. Secondary summer school is printed on the student calendar but sits outside the 176-day regular school year.

planningTips.title: Planning with the Boise School District Calendar
content: Plan a shortened first and last day for K–12; both use early-release schedules rather than full-day dismissal times.
Use the separate Pre-K and ECSE first and last dates and check each reporting or conference day for a Pre-K-specific closure.
For October conferences, match the student's level to the elementary, junior-high, or high-school evening window before scheduling appointments.
Confirm whether the elementary campus uses the standard or late-start schedule because early release is 1:15 p.m. or 1:45 p.m. respectively.
Junior-high families should confirm the exact bell time with the school; the district says times vary by a few minutes and early dismissal depends on the elementary schedule.
Secondary summer-school families should add the two 18-day sessions separately and observe the no-summer-school holiday listed between or within sessions.
Recheck the official calendar page because both PDFs are marked subject to change and a MySchoolDates download does not update automatically.

livingHere.intro: Boise School District is an urban Ada County system whose calendar reflects neighborhood schools, early-learning centers, online and alternative options, and transportation-linked bell schedules.

districtFaqs.q: Do Boise School District K–12 students have a full first day?
districtFaqs.a: No. The official student calendars mark the August 12 K–12 first day as early release. Dismissal depends on school level and elementary schedule.

districtFaqs.q: When do Boise Pre-K and ECSE programs start?
districtFaqs.a: They start after K–12. In 2025–26, Pre-K and ECSE begin August 18; in 2026–27, they begin August 17.

districtFaqs.q: Do all Boise students have no school for fall conferences?
districtFaqs.a: No. The daytime parent-conference closure applies to Pre-K through grade 6. Junior-high and high-school conferences are evening sessions; a separate Friday closure applies districtwide.

districtFaqs.q: What time does Boise elementary school dismiss on early-release days?
districtFaqs.a: Standard elementary campuses dismiss at 1:15 p.m. with lunch served. Campuses on the late-start schedule dismiss at 1:45 p.m. with lunch served.

districtFaqs.q: How many instructional days are on the Boise student calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Both reviewed calendars list 176 instructional days, split into reporting periods of 42, 43, 47, and 44 days.

districtFaqs.q: Does the Boise student calendar include summer school?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. It prints two 18-day Secondary Summer School semesters and identifies a holiday when summer school does not meet. These dates are outside the 176-day regular year.

customSections.content: The official calendar page says ten schools use the late-start elementary schedule but currently enumerates eleven names: Amity, Dallas Harris, Hawthorne, Hillcrest, Lincoln Early Learning Center, Lowell, Morley Nelson, Owyhee, Riverside, Shadow Hills, and Whittier.
